shorts_extract.hook: Most parents assume a quiet toddler is a calm toddler — yet inside Mary Ainsworth's 1970 playroom, the quietest babies hid racing hearts!
shorts_extract.core_experiment: Fifty-six one-year-olds went through eight three-minute room switches with a caregiver, a stranger, two brief goodbyes, and two reunions.
shorts_extract.twist: In 1993, hidden heart monitors and saliva tests proved that silent avoidant toddlers who ignored their returning mother had surging heart rates and spiking stress hormones.

chapters.title: The Quiet-Baby Myth & 1970 Baltimore Playroom
chapters.summary: Contrast two twelve-month-old toddlers in the same sunlit room and introduce Mary Ainsworth and Silvia Bell's 1970 Johns Hopkins experiment.

chapters.title: Before the Strange Situation: Hospital Cribs to Uganda Home Logs
chapters.summary: Why mid-century doctors mistook silent toddlers for 'adjusted' children, and how Bowlby and Ainsworth tracked seventy-two hours of home care per family.

chapters.title: Inside the Eight Three-Minute Episodes
chapters.summary: Walk step-by-step through the stranger's arrival, the two separations, and why reunion — not goodbye — is the real measurement.

chapters.title: Three Patterns: Secure (70%), Avoidant (20%), Ambivalent (10%)
chapters.summary: Compare the thirty-second reunion reset of secure toddlers against ambivalent protest and avoidant toy-turning.

chapters.title: The 1993 Heart-Rate & Cortisol Shock (Spangler & Grossmann)
chapters.summary: Reveal wireless ECG and fifteen-to-thirty-minute salivary cortisol spikes proving avoidant calm is an active mask.

chapters.title: The Amygdala-Prefrontal Co-Regulation Switch & Adult Echoes
chapters.summary: Map Dylan Gee and Nim Tottenham's 2014 fMRI maternal buffering circuit and show how childhood reunions echo in adult conflict.
